title: V3 Question Types Demo
description: One question of each V3 type: balancing, electron configuration, periodic-table pick, significant figures, sorting into groups, labelling a diagram, and reading and plotting a graph.

questions.text: Balance the equation for the formation of water.
questions.explanation: Two H2 molecules react with one O2 molecule to give two H2O molecules.

questions.text: Write the ground-state electron configuration of sodium.
questions.explanation: Sodium has 11 electrons: the neon core plus one 3s electron.

questions.text: Click the two alkali metals that are in periods 3 and 4.
questions.explanation: Alkali metals are in group 1: sodium is in period 3 and potassium is in period 4.

questions.text: Write 0.00450 g in scientific notation using the correct number of significant figures (in grams).
questions.explanation: 0.00450 has three significant figures, so it is 4.50 x 10^-3.

questions.text: Sort each substance by the type of bonding it has.
questions.explanation: Metal + nonmetal gives ionic, two nonmetals give covalent, and a metal on its own is metallic.

questions.text: Place each label on the lab equipment.

image.alt: A lab bench with a beaker on the left, a flask in the middle and a burner on the right

questions.explanation: The beaker is the straight-sided vessel, the flask has the narrow neck.

questions.text: Read the graph: what is the temperature after 4 minutes?
questions.explanation: At 4 minutes the line is at 60 °C.

questions.text: Plot the points (1, 20), (3, 50) and (5, 80) on the grid.
questions.explanation: Each point must land within 0.3 min and 5 °C of its target.
